newsitem.title: UK: Most LIFFE sugar futures drift down in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Most LIFFE sugar futures drift down in quiet trade.

text.p: Most LIFFE sugar futures came down amid low volume in a lacklustre post-holiday session.
The exceptions were December 1997 and March 1998, which were last traded unchanged.
The market was following New York down, traders said. But lower prices in London were not enough to keep up with New York's fall, they said.
Traders described the fall in London as a drift caused by trade selling.
Volume was thin, with front month March dominating business. By 1600 GMT it traded 254 lots of a total 433, last changing hands $2 lower at $307.20 a tonne.
Most of the rest of the volume was on May, which traded 134 lots by 1600 GMT, falling $1.5 to $307.
Traders blamed low volumes on the continued absence of many market players after the new year holiday, combined with the continuing Japanese holiday.
They did not expect active trading before next week.
"To be quite honest, a lot of people have already gone home," one trader said.
